# LITs with `tags` `graphs-and-networks`

*Topics — The twenty-eight kinds of claim this anthology files against — the primary axis of both the practice registry and the reading list, and the same twenty-eight for each (ADR-026). The filing rule is the point: take a domain topic when the claim is ABOUT the domain; a claim merely discovered in one still takes its kind. The axis organizes the record, it does not bound it: content the list cannot place is evidence the list is short (ADR-059).*

**Graphs and networks** — graph-structured data and the models that run on it — node, graph and knowledge-graph embeddings, message passing and graph neural networks, their expressive power and positional encodings, graph transformers, geometric and equivariant GNNs, how they are evaluated, over-smoothing, over-squashing, curvature and rewiring, community structure and partitioning, and language models given graphs.

| [LIT-386](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-386.md) | SuperGlue: Learning Feature Matching with Graph Neural Networks | Sarlin et al. (2019), [ARXIV-1911.11763](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11763). Match two sets of local features by learning the matcher rather than hand-designing it: a graph neural network predicts assignment costs and a differentiable optimal transport step solves them, finding correspondences and rejecting unmatchable points in one operation. Replaces "hand-designed heuristics" with priors over geometry learned end to end — and still consumes keypoints somebody else detected. | Active |
| [LIT-579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-579.md) | Where Did the Gap Go? Reassessing the Long-Range Graph Benchmark | Tönshoff, Ritzert, Rosenbluth, Grohe (2023), [ARXIV-2309.00367](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00367). On the Long-Range Graph Benchmark, graph transformers were reported to beat message-passing GNNs. After a basic hyperparameter sweep within the same 500k-parameter budget, GCN, GINE and GatedGCN all beat GPS on Peptides-func and Peptides-struct. Most of the gain comes from a 2-layer prediction head instead of a linear one. On the superpixel datasets, input feature normalization accounts for at least half the gain of most models, and GPS stays ahead there. The link-prediction metric's code computed raw MRR where the paper specified filtered MRR. | Active |
| [LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md) | How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks? | Xu, Hu, Leskovec, Jegelka (ICLR 2019), [ARXIV-1810.00826](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00826). Message-passing GNNs are at most as discriminative as the 1-WL isomorphism test, and they reach that bound when aggregation and readout are injective on multisets. Sum aggregation with an MLP update (GIN) is; mean (GCN) and max (GraphSAGE) are not. On featureless Reddit graphs, mean-aggregation GNNs are at chance (50.0, 20.0) and GIN scores 92.4 and 57.5. These are validation accuracies averaged over 10 folds, with the epoch chosen on the same folds. Errica et al.'s held-out rerun gives GIN 87.0 and 53.8. On the other seven benchmarks, most differences are within a standard deviation. | Active |
| [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md) | Pitfalls of Graph Neural Network Evaluation | Shchur, Mumme, Bojchevski, Günnemann (R2L workshop, NeurIPS 2018), [ARXIV-1811.05868](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.05868). GCN, GAT, MoNet and GraphSAGE were run with one shared training and tuning procedure, over 100 random splits × 20 seeds on 8 datasets. GCN has the best average rank (2.3) and relative accuracy (99.4%). On Planetoid's single split GAT wins Cora and Citeseer; on another random split of the same sizes GCN wins them. GAT's lower average on Amazon comes from 138 of 2,000 runs collapsing. | Active |
| [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md) | Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks | Kipf and Welling (ICLR 2017), [ARXIV-1609.02907](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02907). The GCN layer is H′ = σ(D̃^{-1/2}ÃD̃^{-1/2} H W), with self-loops added and the adjacency symmetrically normalized. It is motivated as a first-order approximation of spectral graph convolution. Two layers reach 81.5% on Cora, 70.3% on Citeseer and 79.0% on Pubmed, all on the single Planetoid split. Models deeper than about 7 layers are hard to train without residual connections. | Active |
| [LIT-766](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-766.md) | Community Detection on Networks with Ricci Flow | Ni et al. (2019), [ARXIV-1907.03993](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.03993) (Scientific Reports). Ollivier–Ricci curvature on a graph comes from optimal transport between the neighbourhoods of an edge's endpoints. Edges between communities come out negatively curved and edges inside them positively curved. A discrete Ricci flow stretches negative edges and shrinks positive ones, and thresholding the resulting weights ("surgery") separates the communities. On a 500-node, two-block SBM, ARI goes from nearly 100% at p_inter/p_intra = 0.5 to nearly 0% at 0.55. On LFR graphs it is the most stable of the methods compared. | Active |
| [LIT-803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md) | Understanding over-squashing and bottlenecks on graphs via curvature | Topping, Di Giovanni, Chamberlain, Dong, Bronstein (ICLR 2022), [ARXIV-2111.14522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14522). The Jacobian of node i's features with respect to node s's input is bounded by the (r+1)-th power of the normalized adjacency. The paper defines Balanced Forman curvature, a combinatorial edge curvature that lower-bounds Ollivier curvature, and proves that a very negatively curved edge leaves many 2-hop neighbours with a small average Jacobian. SDRF rewires by adding edges around the most negative edge. On nine node-classification sets with a GCN, it beats no rewiring on all nine, by 0.3–6.7 points, while changing 0.2–33% of edges. DIGL or a fully adjacent last layer is ahead of it on five. | Active |
| [LIT-804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-804.md) | Relational inductive biases, deep learning, and graph networks | Battaglia et al., 27 authors from DeepMind, Google Brain, MIT and Edinburgh (2018), [ARXIV-1806.01261](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01261). Part position paper, part review: it argues that combinatorial generalization needs structured representations, and defines the graph network (GN) block, which updates edges, then nodes, then a global attribute, with permutation-invariant aggregations between them. MPNNs, non-local networks and other graph models are written as GN configurations. It reports no new experiments. | Active |
| [LIT-805](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-805.md) | Graph Contrastive Learning with Augmentations | You, Chen, Sui, Chen, Wang, Shen (NeurIPS 2020), [ARXIV-2010.13902](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13902). SimCLR for graph-level GNN pre-training: two augmentations of each graph (node dropping, edge perturbation, attribute masking, random-walk subgraph) as positives, the rest of the batch as negatives. Contrasting without augmentation hurts, and which augmentation helps depends on the data: edge perturbation lowers accuracy on the molecule set NCI1 at every strength tried and raises it on social networks. In transfer to molecular property prediction it has the best mean on 4 of 9 tasks and is below no pre-training on 3. | Active |
| [LIT-806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-806.md) | Deep Graph Infomax | Veličković, Fedus, Hamilton, Liò, Bengio, Hjelm (ICLR 2019), [ARXIV-1809.10341](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.10341). Train a GNN encoder without labels by having a bilinear discriminator tell each node's embedding paired with the graph's mean summary from embeddings of a corrupted graph, made by shuffling node features across positions. A linear probe on the embeddings reaches 82.3% on Cora against 81.5% reported for supervised GCN. A randomly initialized encoder of the same shape is almost as good on the inductive tasks: 0.933 against 0.940 micro-F1 on Reddit, 0.626 against 0.638 on PPI. | Active |
| [LIT-807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md) | Talk like a Graph: Encoding Graphs for Large Language Models | Fatemi, Halcrow, Perozzi (ICLR 2024), [ARXIV-2310.04560](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04560). The paper writes a graph as text in nine ways and asks PaLM 62B and PaLM 2 XXS–L six basic questions about graphs of 5–20 nodes, with five prompting methods (GraphQA). Encoding matters most where an answer needs one node's neighbourhood. On PaLM 62B zero-shot, listing each node's neighbours ("incident") gets 53.8% on connected nodes, against 19.8% for an edge list and 4.0–8.8% for named-entity encodings. It matters little for edge existence, where every PaLM 62B configuration is below the 54% majority, and the edge list beats incident on edge count. The headline "4.8% to 61.8%" is the gap between the best and worst of the nine encodings, not a gain over a sensible default. | Active |
| [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md) | Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs | Hu, Fey, Zitnik, Dong, Ren, Liu, Catasta, Leskovec (NeurIPS 2020), [ARXIV-2005.00687](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00687). Fifteen node, link and graph datasets, from 4k to 111M nodes, each with an application-driven split (time, species, scaffold, protein target, project) and a fixed evaluator. On every dataset where the authors also ran a random split of the same proportions, the same model scores higher on it: 88.2 against 78.5% on ogbn-products, 82.7 against 77.1 ROC-AUC on ogbg-molhiv, 92.9 against 70.4% on ogbg-ppa. | Active |
| [LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md) | node2vec: Scalable Feature Learning for Networks | Grover and Leskovec (KDD 2016), [ARXIV-1607.00653](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.00653). DeepWalk with a second-order biased walk: a return parameter p and an in-out parameter q move the walk between BFS-like and DFS-like exploration, and p = q = 1 is DeepWalk. With p and q picked by grid search on 10% of the labels, Macro-F1 at 50% labeled is 0.2581 against DeepWalk's 0.2110 on BlogCatalog and 0.1552 against 0.1274 on Wikipedia, and 0.1791 against 0.1768 on PPI. For link prediction, a Hadamard product of node vectors beats the common neighbor heuristics, and DeepWalk ties it on Facebook at 0.9680 AUC. | Active |
| [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md) | The Surprising Power of Graph Neural Networks with Random Node Initialization | Abboud, Ceylan, Grohe, Lukasiewicz (IJCAI 2021), [ARXIV-2010.01179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.01179). A message-passing GNN with global readout whose initial node features are partly random can approximate any invariant function on graphs of a fixed size, with high probability, and stays invariant in expectation. On EXP, a synthetic set of 1-WL-indistinguishable pairs, a GCN with random initialization scores 96.6–98.0% against 50% without it. It converges far slower than a 3-WL-class GCN, needs delicate tuning, and is evaluated on no real benchmark. | Active |
| [LIT-811](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-811.md) | A Survey on Oversmoothing in Graph Neural Networks | Rusch, Bronstein, Mishra (2023), [ARXIV-2303.10993](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10993). A short survey that defines over-smoothing as exponential decay with depth of a node-similarity measure, one that is zero exactly when all node features are equal and is subadditive. Dirichlet energy qualifies. Mean Average Distance does not, being zero for any one-dimensional features of one sign. Its key experiment: on Cora, a deep GCN with a bias term keeps its Dirichlet energy constant and loses accuracy with depth just as the plain GCN does, and so does PairNorm. Avoiding over-smoothing is necessary for deep GNNs and not sufficient. | Active |
| [LIT-812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-812.md) | E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks | Satorras, Hoogeboom, Welling (ICML 2021), [ARXIV-2102.09844](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09844). A message-passing layer that also carries a coordinate per node: messages see only squared distances, and coordinates move along a weighted sum of relative position vectors, which is E(n)-equivariant in any dimension without spherical harmonics. On a 3D charged 5-body system it cuts position MSE 32% against the next model (0.0071 vs 0.0104). On QM9 it does not update coordinates, which makes it an invariant distance GNN, and it is competitive rather than best. | Active |
| [LIT-813](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-813.md) | Equivariant Subgraph Aggregation Networks | Bevilacqua, Frasca, Lim, Srinivasan, Cai, Balamurugan, Bronstein, Maron (ICLR 2022), [ARXIV-2110.02910](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.02910). Represents a graph as a bag of its subgraphs (node-deleted, edge-deleted or ego-networks), runs a shared GNN on each, optionally with information shared across the bag, and pools. With a 1-WL encoder this is strictly more expressive than 1-WL. On ZINC12k under 100k parameters, GIN goes from 0.252 to 0.102 MAE. On TUD and OGB the gains over GIN are mostly inside a standard deviation, and with a GCN encoder most variants lower OGB-MOLHIV test AUC. Training costs about 2–3× GIN per epoch. | Active |
| [LIT-814](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-814.md) | Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs | Hamilton, Ying, Leskovec (NIPS 2017), [ARXIV-1706.02216](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02216). GraphSAGE learns aggregator functions over a uniformly sampled, fixed-size neighborhood, so it can embed nodes and whole graphs it never saw in training. Supervised micro-F1 on unseen nodes is 0.839 on a Web of Science citation graph, 0.954 on Reddit and 0.612 on unseen PPI graphs, against 0.575, 0.585 and 0.422 for raw features alone. Each cell is a single run with no spread, and the aggregator significance test rests on six settings. | Active |
| [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md) | GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting | Lam et al. (Science 2023), [ARXIV-2212.12794](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12794). A 36.7M-parameter encode-process-decode GNN on an icosahedral multi-mesh, trained on 39 years of ERA5 to step the global 0.25° state six hours ahead, rolled out to 10 days. Against ECMWF's HRES, each scored on its own analysis, it has lower RMSE on 90.3% of 1,380 variable-level-lead-time targets (89.9% significantly). Most losses are at 50 hPa, which with the levels above it carries 0.66% of the training loss weight. Deterministic only, and its MSE training blurs long-lead forecasts; with both models optimally blurred it still wins 88.0%. | Active |
| [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md) | Deeper Insights into Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Learning | Li, Han, Wu (AAAI 2018), [ARXIV-1801.07606](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07606). A GCN layer is symmetric Laplacian smoothing followed by a linear map. On Cora with 20 labels per class, one smoothing step takes a one-layer network from 53.1% to 70.8%. Repeated without weights, the smoothing converges on each connected component to a vector proportional to √degree, which the paper names over-smoothing. The depth evidence is an untrained GCN on the 34-node karate club. Of its own deeper trained GCNs it says only that accuracy "decreases drastically, which is probably due to overfitting". Co- and self-training raise GCN accuracy at very low label rates. | Active |
| [LIT-817](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-817.md) | Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks | Dwivedi, Joshi, Luu, Laurent, Bengio, Bresson (2020; v5 of 2022 read here), [ARXIV-2003.00982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.00982). Twelve medium-scale datasets and a shared codebase compare GNNs at fixed budgets of 100k and 500k parameters, with four seeds. It introduced Laplacian-eigenvector positional encodings: with random sign flips they cut a 16-layer GatedGCN's ZINC MAE from 0.354 to 0.214, and lift it from 10% to 99.8% on CSL. On three TU datasets, rerunning with a second seed reorders the models. | Active |
| [LIT-818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-818.md) | Sign and Basis Invariant Networks for Spectral Graph Representation Learning | Lim, Robinson, Zhao, Smidt, Sra, Maron, Jegelka (ICLR 2023), [ARXIV-2202.13013](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13013). Eigenvectors are defined only up to sign, and up to a rotation within a repeated eigenvalue. SignNet computes ρ(φ(v)+φ(−v)) per eigenvector and BasisNet works on the projector VVᵀ, so both are invariant by construction. With a GatedGCN on ZINC, Laplacian eigenvectors with random sign flips give 0.198 MAE and SignNet 0.121 on the same 8 eigenvectors, or 0.100 on all of them. Every graph experiment uses SignNet; BasisNet is tested only on fitting synthetic spectral filters. | Active |
| [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md) | RotatE: Knowledge Graph Embedding by Relational Rotation in Complex Space | Sun, Deng, Nie, Tang (ICLR 2019), [ARXIV-1902.10197](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10197). Relations as element-wise rotations of complex entity vectors (t = h ∘ r, \|r_i\| = 1), which can represent symmetry, inversion and composition where TransE cannot represent symmetry. Trained with a new self-adversarial negative sampling. MRR 0.338 on FB15k-237 and 0.476 on WN18RR. Its own ablation re-trains TransE with the same sampling and reaches 0.332 on FB15k-237, so most of the gain over previously reported baselines there is training, not rotation. On FB15k, which needs symmetry, the gap stays: 0.797 against 0.735. | Active |
| [LIT-820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-820.md) | Let Your Graph Do the Talking: Encoding Structured Data for LLMs | Perozzi, Fatemi, Zelle, Tsitsulin, Kazemi, Al-Rfou, Halcrow (2024), [ARXIV-2402.05862](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05862). GraphToken trains a small GNN, separately for each task, whose pooled output is projected into soft tokens and prepended to the prompt of a frozen Flan-PaLM 2 S. On GraphQA it reaches 0.996 on node count, 0.962 on node degree and 0.956 on cycle check, but only 0.264 on connected nodes. Its prompting baselines match, to the digit, Talk like a Graph's PaLM 62B averages over all nine text encodings, a different and larger model. So "up to 73 points" sets a trained encoder against prompts averaged over good and bad encodings. The one same-model trained baseline, a soft prompt with no access to the graph, scores at the majority rate. | Active |
| [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md) | Exphormer: Sparse Transformers for Graphs | Shirzad, Velingker, Venkatachalam, Sutherland, Sinop (ICML 2023), [ARXIV-2303.06147](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06147). Replaces full attention inside GPS with attention over the input edges, a random regular expander graph and a few virtual nodes, O(\|V\|+\|E\|) in all. It beats GPS's Performer and BigBird variants on all four datasets compared and full-attention GPS on CIFAR10 (74.7 against 72.3), and runs ogbn-arxiv (169k nodes), where GPS is out of memory. On LRGB it gains most on PCQM-Contact (MRR 0.364 against 0.334). Which sparse components help is chosen per dataset: the molecular LRGB models use no expander at all. | Active |
| [LIT-822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-822.md) | Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks | Pfaff, Fortunato, Sanchez-Gonzalez, Battaglia (ICLR 2021), [ARXIV-2010.03409](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03409). MeshGraphNets: an encode-process-decode graph network that passes messages along simulation-mesh edges and, for deforming bodies, along world-space proximity edges, trained on one-step targets with input noise and rolled out for hundreds of steps. It beats a grid U-Net, a GCN and the particle model GNS on cloth, plates and 2D flows, and can learn the remesher's sizing field. The quoted 11–290× speedup is a GPU model against CPU solvers; on the same CPU it is 4–22×. | Active |
| [LIT-823](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-823.md) | On Over-Squashing in Message Passing Neural Networks: The Impact of Width, Depth, and Topology | Di Giovanni, Giusti, Barbero, Luise, Liò, Bronstein (ICML 2023), [ARXIV-2302.02941](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.02941). A theory paper. The sensitivity of node v to node u after m layers is at most (c_σ·w·p)^m times the (v, u) entry of the m-th power of the message-passing matrix. Width p and weight scale can raise the bound, but for the whole network at once. With depth near the distance, over-squashing hits distant, badly connected nodes. With much more depth, gradients vanish. Averaged over layers, the obstruction between two nodes is bounded above and below by their commute time, under an assumption that every path is active with equal probability. The experiments are synthetic. | Active |
| [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md) | Network Embedding as Matrix Factorization: Unifying DeepWalk, LINE, PTE, and node2vec | Qiu, Dong, Ma, Li, Wang, Tang (WSDM 2018), [ARXIV-1710.02971](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02971). Carries Levy and Goldberg's SGNS result to graphs. As walks grow long, DeepWalk with negative sampling factorizes log(vol(G)/T · Σ_{r=1..T} (D⁻¹A)^r D⁻¹) − log b, and LINE is the case T = 1. Computing that matrix, truncating it at log 1 and taking an SVD (NetMF) beats DeepWalk on BlogCatalog, PPI and Flickr with few labels, by up to 50.71% relative Micro-F1 on PPI at 10%. It loses to LINE on Flickr and ties DeepWalk on Wikipedia Macro-F1. | Active |
| [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md) | SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions | Schütt et al. (NeurIPS 2017), [ARXIV-1706.08566](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.08566). Message passing over atoms whose filters are generated by a network from interatomic distances, so the energy is rotation-invariant and smooth, and forces taken as its negative gradient are energy-conserving. QM9 U0 MAE 0.31 kcal/mol at 110k training molecules. On MD17 with 1,000 configurations, training on energies and forces cuts force MAE 17–46× against energies alone (benzene 14.12 → 0.31 kcal/mol/Å), and beats energy-only training on 50,000 on forces. The kernel baseline GDML still has the lower force error on 6 of 8 molecules. | Active |
| [LIT-826](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-826.md) | Graph Attention Networks | Veličković, Cucurull, Casanova, Romero, Liò, Bengio (ICLR 2018), [ARXIV-1710.10903](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10903). Each node attends over its first-order neighbors with softmax-normalized, multi-head attention scores, so neighbors get learned weights instead of fixed degree-based ones. Over 100 runs on the Planetoid split it scores 83.0% on Cora and 72.5% on Citeseer against 81.4% and 70.9% for a 64-unit GCN, and ties on Pubmed. On unseen PPI graphs it reaches micro-F1 0.973, against 0.934 for the same model with constant attention. | Active |
| [LIT-827](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-827.md) | Graph Neural Networks Exponentially Lose Expressive Power for Node Classification | Oono, Suzuki (ICLR 2020), [ARXIV-1905.10947](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10947). For a ReLU GCN, the distance of layer-l features from the subspace that carries only connected-component and degree information is at most (sλ)^l times its initial value. Here s bounds the weights' largest singular values, and λ < 1 is set by the augmented normalized Laplacian's spectrum. On dense Erdős–Rényi graphs most GCNs meet the condition. On real citation graphs the theorem says something only for 1 ≤ s < 1.0036 (Cora), so the experiments add random edges to raise the threshold to 1.11–1.17. | Active |
| [LIT-828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-828.md) | MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields | Batatia, Kovács, Simm, Ortner, Csányi (NeurIPS 2022), [ARXIV-2206.07697](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07697). MACE builds each message as a symmetric tensor product of a neighbor sum, so one layer carries up to four-body correlations at roughly pairwise cost, and two layers suffice where two-body equivariant models need four to six. On 3BPA at 1200 K its force RMSE is 62.0 meV/Å against NequIP's 76.2, at about a quarter of NequIP's latency in the authors' code. On aspirin, raising body order steepens the learning curve (slopes −0.33, −0.51, −0.64) and, at body order four, adding equivariant features does not (−0.64, −0.63, −0.64). | Active |
| [LIT-829](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-829.md) | Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry | Gilmer, Schoenholz, Riley, Vinyals, Dahl (ICML 2017), [ARXIV-1704.01212](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01212). Message Passing Neural Networks name the common form of eight earlier graph models: T rounds of messages summed over neighbors, a node update, and a permutation-invariant readout. An MPNN with edge-network messages, set2set readout and explicit hydrogens reaches chemical accuracy on 11 of 13 QM9 targets, with an average error ratio of 0.68 against 1.35 for the best hand-engineered baseline. That is one random split, with no repeated runs. | Active |
| [LIT-830](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-830.md) | Can Language Models Solve Graph Problems in Natural Language? | Wang, Feng, He, Tan, Han, Tsvetkov (NeurIPS 2023), [ARXIV-2305.10037](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10037). NLGraph is a benchmark of 29,370 synthetic graph problems in natural language over eight tasks. Its standard set (5,902 problems) is used with text-davinci-003. With chain of thought (CoT), the model averages 84.6% on connectivity and 66.8% on cycle detection, where random is 50%. On topological sort, maximum flow, bipartite matching and Hamilton path, CoT, least-to-most and self-consistency mostly fail to beat plain few-shot or zero-shot prompting. When the two queried nodes are the degree-1 ends of a chain, CoT accuracy is 44.5 points below the general set. The paper's Build-a-Graph instruction adds 5.7 points on cycle and 4.3 on shortest path, and nothing on Hamilton path. | Active |
| [LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md) | LINE: Large-scale Information Network Embedding | Tang, Qu, Wang, Zhang, Yan, Mei (WWW 2015), [ARXIV-1503.03578](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.03578). Two objectives for embedding large weighted or directed graphs: first-order (linked nodes close) and second-order (nodes with similar neighbor distributions close, skip-gram with negative sampling over edges). Sampling edges in proportion to weight instead of multiplying gradients by it is what makes weighted graphs trainable: on a Wikipedia word network with a billion edges, analogy accuracy is 66.10% with edge sampling and 14.49% without. On sparse YouTube, second-order alone loses to DeepWalk. | Active |
| [LIT-832](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-832.md) | E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials | Batzner et al. (Nature Communications 2022), [ARXIV-2101.03164](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03164). NequIP: a message-passing interatomic potential whose features are O(3) tensors up to order l, combined by Clebsch–Gordan tensor products with spherical- harmonic filters, with forces as the gradient of the energy. On MD17 with 1,000 configurations, aspirin force MAE 8.2 meV/Å against SchNet's 58.5. The same network with only l = 0 features scores 41.9 on revised MD17, and 12.9 at l = 1. The equivariant variants also show a steeper log-log learning curve than the invariant one, on water and aspirin, read from figures. "1000× fewer data" is a force-error comparison against an older, non-smooth DeepMD; on energies DeepMD stays ahead. | Active |
| [LIT-833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md) | Graph Neural Networks with Learnable Structural and Positional Representations | Dwivedi, Luu, Laurent, Bengio, Bresson (ICLR 2022), [ARXIV-2110.07875](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07875). Introduces random-walk positional encodings (RWPE, a node's probability of returning to itself in 1..k steps) and LSPE, which updates the positional channel in every layer. On ZINC, GatedGCN goes from 0.251 MAE with no encoding to 0.090. The controlled ablation puts most of that in the input encoding: RWPE at the input alone gives 0.122, against 0.202 for Laplacian eigenvectors. Learning the positional channel adds 0.122 to 0.093. Gains on OGB molecules are under 2%. | Active |
| [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md) | Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data | Bordes, Usunier, Garcia-Durán, Weston, Yakhnenko (NeurIPS 2013). Embed knowledge-base entities and relations in one space so that h + r ≈ t, and train with a margin ranking loss against triples with the head or tail replaced. One vector per relation, so far fewer parameters than the matrix-per-relation models it beats. Filtered hits@10 is 89.2% on WN and 47.1% on FB15k, against 81.6% and 44.1% for the best baselines. It introduced the FB15k benchmark and the filtered evaluation setting. | Active |
| [LIT-835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-835.md) | Improving Graph Neural Network Expressivity via Subgraph Isomorphism Counting | Bouritsas, Frasca, Zafeiriou, Bronstein (TPAMI 2023), [ARXIV-2006.09252](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09252). Counts small substructures (cycles, paths, cliques) around each node or edge in preprocessing and feeds the counts into message passing. This is strictly more expressive than 1-WL for any substructure other than a star, and stays linear in edges at training time. ZINC test MAE 0.140 without edge features against 0.254 for the same MPNN. Training error tracks how uniquely the counts identify nodes; test error does not, and cycles generalize best on molecules. | Active |
| [LIT-836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md) | Position: Graph Foundation Models are Already Here | Mao, Chen, Tang, Zhao, Ma, Zhao, Shah, Galkin, Tang (ICML 2024, position paper), [ARXIV-2402.02216](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02216). A graph foundation model needs a "graph vocabulary": units of graph structure that keep their meaning across datasets, so training on many graphs transfers positively. The paper reviews network-analysis, expressiveness and stability principles for node classification, link prediction and graph classification, and then data scaling, model scaling and the use of LLMs. It runs no experiments. The text qualifies the title: no existing model transfers across all graph tasks and domains, and the conclusion calls a universal one challenging. What is "here" is task- and domain-specific models such as ULTRA for knowledge-graph completion. | Active |
| [LIT-837](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-837.md) | DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations | Perozzi, Al-Rfou, Skiena (KDD 2014), [ARXIV-1403.6652](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.6652). Treat truncated random walks on a graph as sentences and train skip-gram with hierarchical softmax on them; the word vectors are node embeddings. With one-vs-rest logistic regression on top, they beat spectral, modularity, EdgeCluster and wvRN features when few nodes are labeled: Micro-F1 32.4 against 27.43 for the best baseline at 1% of Flickr, and 37.95 against 26.79 at 1% of YouTube. On BlogCatalog, spectral clustering is ahead from 70% labeled on. | Active |
| [LIT-838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-838.md) | A Fair Comparison of Graph Neural Networks for Graph Classification | Errica, Podda, Bacciu, Micheli (ICLR 2020), [ARXIV-1912.09893](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09893). Five GNNs were re-run on nine graph-classification benchmarks, in more than 47,000 training runs, with the same features, stratified 10-fold splits, and hyperparameters selected inside each training fold. On D&D, PROTEINS and ENZYMES no GNN beats a baseline that ignores the graph: 78.4, 75.8 and 65.2% for the baseline, against at most 76.6, 73.7 and 59.6%. GIN's published accuracies were validation, not test, scores. | Active |
| [LIT-839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-839.md) | On the Bottleneck of Graph Neural Networks and its Practical Implications | Alon, Yahav (ICLR 2021), [ARXIV-2006.05205](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05205). A node's receptive field grows exponentially with depth, and its messages must squeeze into a fixed-size vector. The paper calls this over-squashing. On a synthetic tree task, GCN and GIN stop fitting the training set at depth 4 (GCN 70%), and GAT and GGNN at depth 5. Making only the last layer fully adjacent, with no new weights and no retuning, cuts QM9 error by 42% on average over six GNNs, against 5.5% from doubling the width. The gains on NCI1, ENZYMES and VarMisuse are smaller and often within one standard deviation. | Active |
| [LIT-840](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-840.md) | Weisfeiler and Leman Go Neural: Higher-order Graph Neural Networks | Morris, Ritzert, Fey, Hamilton, Lenssen, Rattan, Grohe (AAAI 2019), [ARXIV-1810.02244](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.02244). Proves, independently of GIN and three days after it, that no message-passing GNN separates more graphs than 1-WL, and that a plain sum-aggregation layer with suitably chosen weights matches 1-WL on a given graph. Proposes k-GNNs, which pass messages between k-element node sets. On QM9 the hierarchical 1-2-3-GNN lowers MAE against a 1-GNN on 11 of 12 targets, by 54.45% averaged over all 12. Its TUD accuracy gains over the 1-GNN are 1.8–3.9 points, reported without deviations. | Active |
| [LIT-841](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-841.md) | One for All: Towards Training One Graph Model for All Classification Tasks | Liu, Feng, Kong, Liang, Tao, Chen, Zhang (ICLR 2024), [ARXIV-2310.00149](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00149). OFA describes every node and edge in text and embeds it with one language model. It adds a task "prompt node" and one node per class to the graph, and trains a single R-GCN-style GNN on nine datasets at once. Jointly trained, it beats the best of GCN, GAT and GIN on 8 of 10 supervised tasks. The large gains are on knowledge-graph relation classification (WN18RR 96.91% against 67.40%), and a separately trained OFA gets those too (97.22%). On Cora nodes it is below GAT (75.90% against 82.76%). Zero-shot transfer to unseen graphs is weak: AUC 35.67 on HIV, below chance, and 30.96% on 5-way WN18RR. | Active |
| [LIT-842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-842.md) | Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer | Rampášek, Galkin, Dwivedi, Luu, Wolf, Beaini (NeurIPS 2022), [ARXIV-2205.12454](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12454). A graph-transformer layer that sums a local message-passing layer and a global attention layer, then applies an MLP, on node features carrying positional or structural encodings. Removing the message-passing layer hurts on all six ablated datasets (ZINC MAE 0.070 to 0.217). Removing attention matters less (ZINC unchanged, Peptides-func AP 0.654 to 0.616). ZINC MAE 0.070 and the LRGB results were state of the art when published. The best results use full quadratic attention, not the linear attention in the title. | Active |
| [LIT-843](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-843.md) | Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation? | Ying, Cai, Luo, Zheng, Ke, He, Shen, Liu (NeurIPS 2021), [ARXIV-2106.05234](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05234). A standard Transformer over all nodes, given node degree as an input embedding and a learned attention bias per shortest-path distance and per edge feature along the path. On PCQM4M-LSC it reaches validation MAE 0.1234 against GIN-VN's 0.1395, an 11.5% relative cut, with 7× the parameters; an ensemble won the OGB-LSC graph track. In a shorter ablation run the encodings take MAE from 0.2276 to 0.1304. At a matched 500k budget on ZINC it reaches MAE 0.122. | Active |
| [LIT-844](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-844.md) | Long Range Graph Benchmark | Dwivedi, Rampášek, Galkin, Parviz, Wolf, Luu, Beaini (NeurIPS 2022 Datasets and Benchmarks), [ARXIV-2206.08164](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08164). Five datasets meant to need long-range interaction: PascalVOC-SP, COCO-SP, PCQM-Contact, Peptides-func and Peptides-struct. Peptides graphs average 150.9 nodes and diameter 57.0. At a 500k-parameter budget, transformers beat the best message-passing model on Peptides-func (AP 0.644 against 0.607) and Peptides-struct (MAE 0.253 against 0.336). The baselines were sized to the budget, not tuned, and [LIT-579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-579.md) later closed both Peptides gaps. | Active |
